in_hebrew.name: פרודנטיה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם פרודנטיה מתאר אדם חכם ודבריו מדויקים. הוא נצרך מהמילה הלטינית prudentia, העוסקת בחוכמה ובחיים תבוניים. השם קשור בהשגחה ובחשבון שהאל מגזר באיחוד. זאת תכונה חשובה לכל נוצרי, ובמיוחד למבוגרים, שבאמצעותה יוכלו לעשות בחירות חכמות.

in_greek.name: Πρωτεντία
in_greek.long_meaning: Ὁ ὀνόματος Πρωτεντία ἀναφέρεται στόν ἀνθρώπινο ἐπιχείρημα σοφίας, σκέψης, και σαφηνείας. Ἀπαρχόμενο ἀπό τὴν Λατινική λέξη prudentia, ἡ Πρωτεντία συνδέεται με τὴν γνῶσιν καὶ τὴν σοφία τῶν Χριστιανῶν. Ἀπὸ τὴν ἴδια Ὀρθόδοξη καὶ Καθολική παράδοση, τὸ ὀνόμα Πρωτεντία ἔχει ὑποδηλωτές τὴν σοφίαν καὶ τὴν σαφήνειαν τοῦ Θεοῦ.

in_latin.name: Prudentia
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Prudentia significat hominem sapientem, prudentem, et perspicacem. Ex radicibus prudentia, Prudentia conectitur cum sapientia et prudentia Christianorum. Ab eadem orthodoxa et catholica traditione, nomen Prudentia indicat sapientiam et perspicaciam Dei.

in_english.name: Prudentia
in_english.meaning: wise, prudent, and discerning person, with careful consideration
in_english.long_meaning: The name Prudentia refers to a wise, prudent, and discerning person, with careful consideration. Derived from the Latin word prudentia, Prudentia is associated with the wisdom and discernment of Christians. In both Orthodox and Catholic traditions, the name Prudentia signifies the wisdom and discernment of God. It reflects the importance of careful consideration and wise decision-making in Christian life, which is essential for spiritual growth and maturity.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Prudentia' carries a rich history and cultural significance, echoing the ancient Roman values of wisdom and caution. This name has been passed down through generations, honoring individuals who have demonstrated foresight, good judgment, and responsible decision-making.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian theology, Prudentia is regarded as a guiding virtue, helping us navigate the complexities of life and make choices in line with God's teachings. As one of the Cardinal Virtues, Prudentia, along with Fortitude, Justice, and Temperance, enables us to strive for moral excellence and draw closer to God. This name serves as a constant reminder to be wise in our actions, thoughtful in our decisions, and humbly submissive to God's divine will.
